# 1 Samuel Chapter 15 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 158v–159r | **Source Image:** 1SA_015_page_001.jpg, 1SA_015_page_002.jpg, 1SA_015_page_003.jpg

---

**1** And Samuel said to Saul, "The LORD sent me to anoint you as king over His people, over Israel. And now, listen to the voice of the words of the LORD.
**2** Thus says the LORD of hosts: 'I have taken account of what Amalek did to Israel, how he set himself against him on the way when he came up from Egypt.
**3** Now go and strike Amalek, and utterly destroy all that belongs to him, and do not spare him; but put to death both man and woman, child and infant, ox and sheep, camel and donkey.'"
**4** And Saul summoned the people and numbered them in Telaim: two hundred thousand foot soldiers and ten thousand men of Judah.
**5** And Saul came to the city of Amalek and lay in wait in the valley.
**6** And Saul said to the Kenites, "Go, depart, go down from among the Amalekites, lest I destroy you with them; for you showed faithful love to all the sons of Israel when they came up from Egypt." And the Kenites departed from among the Amalekites.
**7** And Saul struck the Amalekites from Havilah as you come to Shur, which is east of Egypt.
**8** And he captured Agag the king of the Amalekites alive, and all the people he utterly destroyed with the edge of the sword.
**9** But Saul and the people spared Agag and the best of the sheep and the cattle and the fatlings and the lambs, and all that was good, and they were not willing to utterly destroy them. But every despised and worthless thing — that they utterly destroyed.
**10** And the word of the LORD came to Samuel, saying,
**11** "I regret that I made Saul king, for he has turned back from following Me, and My words he has not carried out." And it was grievous to Samuel, and he cried out to the LORD all night.
**12** And Samuel rose early to meet Saul in the morning. And it was told to Samuel, saying, "Saul came to Carmel, and behold, he set up a monument for himself; then he turned and passed on and went down to Gilgal."
**13** And Samuel came to Saul, and Saul said to him, "Blessed are you to the LORD; I have carried out the word of the LORD."
**14** And Samuel said, "Then what is this sound of sheep in my ears, and the sound of cattle that I am hearing?"
**15** And Saul said, "They brought them from the Amalekites, for the people spared the best of the sheep and the cattle in order to sacrifice to the LORD your God; and the rest we utterly destroyed."
**16** And Samuel said to Saul, "Cease, and I will tell you what the LORD spoke to me this night." And he said to him, "Speak."
**17** And Samuel said, "Is it not so that though you were small in your own eyes, you were made head of the tribes of Israel? And the LORD anointed you as king over Israel.
**18** And the LORD sent you on a journey and said, 'Go, and utterly destroy the sinners, the Amalekites, and fight against them until they are consumed.'
**19** And why did you not listen to the voice of the LORD, but you rushed upon the spoil and did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD?"
**20** And Saul said to Samuel, "Indeed, I did listen to the voice of the LORD, and I went on the journey on which the LORD sent me, and I brought Agag the king of Amalek, and the Amalekites I utterly destroyed.
**21** But the people took from the spoil sheep and cattle, the best of the devoted things, to sacrifice to the LORD your God in Gilgal."
**22** And Samuel said, "Does the LORD delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices as in listening to the voice of the LORD? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, to give heed than the fat of rams.
**23** For rebellion is as the sin of divination, and stubbornness is as iniquity and idolatry. Because you have rejected the word of the LORD, He has also rejected you from being king."
**24** And Saul said to Samuel, "I have sinned, for I have transgressed the command of the LORD and your words, because I feared the people and listened to their voice.
**25** And now, please bear my sin and return with me, that I may worship the LORD."
**26** And Samuel said to Saul, "I will not return with you, for you have rejected the word of the LORD, and the LORD has rejected you from being king over Israel."
**27** And Samuel turned to go, and he seized the edge of his robe, and it tore.
**28** And Samuel said to him, "The LORD has torn the kingdom of Israel from you today, and has given it to your neighbor who is better than you.
**29** And also the Glory of Israel will not lie and will not relent, for He is not a man that He should relent."
**30** And he said, "I have sinned; yet honor me now, please, before the elders of my people and before Israel, and return with me, that I may worship the LORD your God."
**31** And Samuel turned back after Saul, and Saul worshipped the LORD.
**32** And Samuel said, "Bring near to me Agag the king of the Amalekites." And Agag came to him in fetters. And Agag said, "Surely the bitterness of death has turned aside."
**33** And Samuel said, "As your sword has bereaved women, so shall your mother be bereaved among women." And Samuel hewed Agag in pieces before the LORD in Gilgal.
**34** And Samuel went to Ramah, and Saul went up to his house in Gibeah of Saul.
**35** And Samuel did not see Saul again until the day of his death, for Samuel mourned for Saul. And the LORD regretted that He had made Saul king over Israel.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

All three translators agreed on the verse count (35 verses) and narrative structure for this chapter. SOPHIA follows the LOGOS formal-equivalence rendering as the baseline consensus, adopting PNEUMA's phrasing where it demonstrably improves clarity without sacrificing accuracy. Key terms and theological vocabulary were consistently rendered across all three translations.

---
## ⚠️ Disagreement Log

### Verse 2
- **EMET:** "Thus says YHWH of-hosts: 'I-have-attended-to [paqadti] what Amalek did to-Israel, [how] he-set against-him in-the-way when-he-came-up from-Egypt."
- **LOGOS:** "Thus says the LORD of hosts: 'I have taken account of what Amalek did to Israel, how he set himself against him on the way when he came up from Egypt."
- **PNEUMA:** "This is what the LORD of Armies says: 'I will punish Amalek for what they did to Israel — how they ambushed them on the road as they came up from Egyp..."
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 3
- **EMET:** "Now go and-strike Amalek and-devote-to-destruction [ha-charamtem] all that [is]-to-him, and-do-not spare him: and-put-to-death from-man unto-woman, fr..."
- **LOGOS:** "Now go and strike Amalek, and utterly destroy all that belongs to him, and do not spare him; but put to death both man and woman, child and infant, ox..."
- **PNEUMA:** "Now go and attack the Amalekites. Completely destroy everything that belongs to them. Do not spare them. Kill men and women, children and infants, cat..."
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 5
- **EMET:** "And-came Saul unto [the]-city of-Amalek and-lay-in-wait [va-yarev] in-the-wadi."
- **LOGOS:** "And Saul came to the city of Amalek and lay in wait in the valley."
- **PNEUMA:** "Saul advanced to the city of Amalek and set an ambush in the valley."
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 6
- **EMET:** "And-said Saul to-the-Kenite, "Go, depart, go-down from-among the-Amalekites, lest I-destroy you with-them, for you showed lovingkindness [hesed] with-..."
- **LOGOS:** "And Saul said to the Kenites, "Go, depart, go down from among the Amalekites, lest I destroy you with them; for you showed faithful love to all the so..."
- **PNEUMA:** "He sent a warning to the Kenites: "Go, leave! Withdraw from among the Amalekites, so I don't destroy you along with them. For you showed kindness to a..."
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 7
- **EMET:** "And-struck Saul Amalek from-Havilah [as]-you-come to-Shur, which [is] upon [the]-face of-Egypt."
- **LOGOS:** "And Saul struck the Amalekites from Havilah as you come to Shur, which is east of Egypt."
- **PNEUMA:** "Then Saul struck down the Amalekites from Havilah all the way to Shur, east of Egypt."
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 9
- **EMET:** "And-spared Saul and-the-people Agag and-the-best of-the-sheep and-the-cattle and-the-fatlings and-the-lambs and-all the-good, and-they-were-not-willin..."
- **LOGOS:** "But Saul and the people spared Agag and the best of the sheep and the cattle and the fatlings and the lambs, and all that was good, and they were not ..."
- **PNEUMA:** "However, Saul and the troops spared Agag, along with the best of the sheep, the cattle, the fattened calves, the lambs — everything that was good. The..."
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 13
- **EMET:** "And-came Samuel to-Saul, and-said Saul to-him, "Blessed [are]-you to-YHWH. I-have-established the-word of-YHWH.""
- **LOGOS:** "And Samuel came to Saul, and Saul said to him, "Blessed are you to the LORD; I have carried out the word of the LORD.""
- **PNEUMA:** "When Samuel reached him, Saul said, "The LORD bless you! I have carried out the LORD's instructions.""
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 16
- **EMET:** "And-said Samuel to-Saul, "Cease, and-I-will-tell you what YHWH spoke to-me the-night." And-he-said to-him, "Speak.""
- **LOGOS:** "And Samuel said to Saul, "Cease, and I will tell you what the LORD spoke to me this night." And he said to him, "Speak.""
- **PNEUMA:** "Samuel said to Saul, "Stop! Let me tell you what the LORD said to me last night." Saul replied, "Speak.""
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 17
- **EMET:** "And-said Samuel, "Is-it-not [that] though-small you [were] in-your-own-eyes, [you are the]-head of-the-tribes of-Israel? And-YHWH anointed you [as]-ki..."
- **LOGOS:** "And Samuel said, "Is it not so that though you were small in your own eyes, you were made head of the tribes of Israel? And the LORD anointed you as k..."
- **PNEUMA:** "Samuel said, "Even though you considered yourself insignificant, were you not made the head of the tribes of Israel? The LORD anointed you king over I..."
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 19
- **EMET:** "And-why did-you-not obey the-voice of-YHWH? And-you-rushed to the-spoil and-did the-evil in-[the]-eyes of-YHWH.""
- **LOGOS:** "And why did you not listen to the voice of the LORD, but you rushed upon the spoil and did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD?""
- **PNEUMA:** "Why did you not obey the LORD? Why did you pounce on the plunder and do what was evil in the LORD's sight?""
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 21
- **EMET:** "And-the-people took from-the-spoil sheep and-cattle, the-best of-the-devoted-things, to-sacrifice to-YHWH your-God in-Gilgal.""
- **LOGOS:** "But the people took from the spoil sheep and cattle, the best of the devoted things, to sacrifice to the LORD your God in Gilgal.""
- **PNEUMA:** "The soldiers took sheep and cattle from the plunder — the best of what was set apart for destruction — to sacrifice to the LORD your God at Gilgal.""
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 24
- **EMET:** "And-said Saul to-Samuel, "I-have-sinned, for I-transgressed the-command of-YHWH and-your-words, for I-feared the-people and-I-obeyed their-voice."
- **LOGOS:** "And Saul said to Samuel, "I have sinned, for I have transgressed the command of the LORD and your words, because I feared the people and listened to t..."
- **PNEUMA:** "Then Saul said to Samuel, "I have sinned. I violated the LORD's command and your instructions. I was afraid of the troops, so I gave in to them."
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 29
- **EMET:** "And-also the-Glory [Netsach] of-Israel will-not lie and-will-not relent [yinnachem], for not a-man He [is] to-relent.""
- **LOGOS:** "And also the Glory of Israel will not lie and will not relent, for He is not a man that He should relent.""
- **PNEUMA:** "Moreover, the Glory of Israel does not lie or change his mind, for he is not a human being who changes his mind.""
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 31
- **EMET:** "And-returned Samuel after Saul, and-worshiped Saul to-YHWH."
- **LOGOS:** "And Samuel turned back after Saul, and Saul worshipped the LORD."
- **PNEUMA:** "So Samuel went back with Saul, and Saul worshiped the LORD."
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 35
- **EMET:** "And-Samuel did-not add to-see Saul until the-day of-his-death, for Samuel mourned for-Saul. And-YHWH regretted [nicham] that He-had-made Saul king ove..."
- **LOGOS:** "And Samuel did not see Saul again until the day of his death, for Samuel mourned for Saul. And the LORD regretted that He had made Saul king over Isra..."
- **PNEUMA:** "Samuel never went to see Saul again for the rest of his life, though Samuel grieved over him. And the LORD regretted that he had made Saul king over I..."
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.

— SOPHIA
